item.title: Project Eleven, Relm Explore Quantum Risk in Digital Asset Insurance
item.description: (Image source: Project Eleven website.) Project Eleven (New York) has named Relm Insurance a development partner for Strongpoint, its institutional digital asset custody product, as the companies explore how post-quantum security controls could be evaluated within insurance underwriting. Project Eleven says a sufficiently capable quantum computer could eventually derive private keys from exposed public keys, creating a potential threat to digital assets. Bringing Underwriting Into Quantum Readiness Relm and Project Eleven will examine factors including key exposure, signing systems, transaction approvals, migration readiness and third-party dependencies.

item.title: Insurer Rolls Out Policy to Protect Data Centers Against Growing Backlash
item.description: Intensifying public pushback against artificial intelligence data centers is spurring a new line of business for a New York-based boutique insurer. Arbol, which was founded by a former Citadel strategist, on Tuesday launched a new policy that protects data center developers and financiers against government-imposed moratoriums that halt or suspend construction. “Data center development has a new and fast-growing risk, and until now there was no way to transfer it,” said Siddhartha Jha, Arbol’s chief executive officer.

item.title: AAA Survey Reveals Disconnect in Drivers’ Obeying ‘Slow Down, Move Over’ Laws
item.description: Though more than 90% of drivers reported moving over and/or slowing down the last time they passed a disabled vehicle, tow truck, or police car on the shoulder, previous AAA FTS research found that only 64% of vehicles subject to Slow Down, Move Over laws were observed changing lanes and/or reducing speed; 36% did neither. We all have a responsibility to keep Roadside Heroes safe as they rescue people.” When Slow Down, Move Over laws were explained, 90% of drivers supported them, and only 2% opposed them. When drivers encounter a vehicle stopped along the roadside, they need to respond right away — because failing to slow down or move over can turn a standard stop into a preventable tragedy.” Closing the gap begins with public education across multiple channels.

item.title: PERILS lifts July European convective storms insured market loss estimate to €2.8bn
item.description: PERILS will also publish a third estimate of the market loss from the mid-July severe convective storms on January 19th, 2027, six months after the event end date. At the same time, CatIQ, Canada’s insured loss and exposure indices provider and subsidiary of PERILS, has published its second industry loss estimate for the severe convective storms that struck southern Ontario, including Toronto, on September 2nd and 3rd, 2026, lifting the total to CAD $671 million. Catastrophe data aggregator PERILS AG has updated its estimate of insurance industry losses for the severe convective storms (SCS) that swept across Germany, France, Switzerland, and Italy in Europe between July 13th and 19th, 2026, lifting the total to EUR 2.806 billion.

item.title: Meta’s Muse AI agents could pose longer-term risk to loss costs: Autonomous
item.description: Meta’s Muse AI agents may pose a longer-term risk to loss costs if savvy consumers use them to navigate, and potentially litigate, insurance claims, according to Autonomous analysts. In a recent report, Autonomous put Meta’s Muse to work across shopping, payments, deposit management, investing and insurance to assess what AI assistants can do with consumers’ money today. However, Autonomous noted that although Muse could help consumers become smarter insurance buyers, it does not yet outperform an insurance agent.

item.title: AI Accelerates Cyber Threat Landscape, Poses New Risks for Insurers and Businesses
item.description: Not to mention, of course, the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence across business operations presents some new ripples in the cyber-risk landscape. Blake Feldman, head of the carrier channel cyber incident response at Integreon, said AI is “an arms race.” The technology is being woven into cyber defense tools, but it is also being used by threat actors to access new systems easier – and perform reconnaissance on victims. Industry executives speaking during a recent NetDiligence Cyber Risk Summit in Philadelphia said cyber losses are increasingly driven by operational disruptions, sophisticated fraud schemes, rather than traditional ransomware and data breaches alone.

item.title: French Riots Seen as Insurance Test Before New Regime Kicks In
item.description: The damage wrought cross France by the recent street riots will demonstrate the extent of current insurance coverage, just months before a new state-backed system kicks in, according to DBRS Morningstar analysts. The new regime “should reduce uncertainty surrounding the allocation of extreme riot losses” once implemented, though French insurers “remain reliant on the existing combination of private insurance, reinsurance and potentially contentious state recourse” until then. “The latest French unrest reinforces a broader trend we already identified in 2023: riots and civil commotion increasingly exhibit characteristics traditionally associated with catastrophe risks,” DBRS Morningstar analysts Marcos Alvarez and Elisabeth Rudman said in a note published Tuesday.

item.title: Home Insurance Tops Property Taxes in Squeeze for US Households
item.description: When that is added to home insurance premiums, the combination is now more expensive than property taxes in 75% of the nation’s counties. Home insurance rates have risen so dramatically over the last decade that the average premium now exceeds the average property-tax bill in two-thirds of US counties, according to an analysis published Monday by Bloomberg Intelligence. Southeastern states have some of the country’s lowest property taxes, and there, insurance premiums can now run 2.5 to 4 times the tax levy.

item.title: Insurers Adopt Property-Level Fire Suppression Analytics
item.description: Property-level fire suppression analytics enable insurers to assess individual risk characteristics beyond traditional community-wide classifications, improving underwriting precision. At the same time, advances in cloud computing, geospatial analytics, and artificial intelligence now make it possible to evaluate fire suppression characteristics at the individual property level rather than relying primarily on community-wide averages. Those measures remain valuable, but they also reflect an era when insurers had far less visibility into fire suppression at the individual property level.

item.title: AI Shapes Customer Demand While Measuring It
item.description: AI systems now shape customer choices through recommendations and interactions, making causal identification essential to distinguish genuine needs from system-influenced demand. The same distinction applies to customer demand: observing what customers choose is not the same as understanding why that choice emerged. How much of the demand we observe reflects what the customer already needed, and how much emerged through the interaction itself?

item.description: Over the past decade, property/casualty carriers made serious and necessary investments in front-end digital transformation. item.title: California Orders Lenders to Report on Handling of Insurance Payouts to LA Fire Victims
item.description: California officials on Thursday ordered mortgage lenders, including banks and credit unions, to report how they have handled insurance payouts to survivors of the 2025 Los Angeles-area fires. The California Business and Consumer Services Agency and the Department of Financial Protection and Innovation want to speed the release of insurance proceeds lenders hold before distributing them to homeowners. Gavin Newsom wrote to bankers’ associations and credit unions, saying homeowners rebuilding after fires reported that lenders sometimes held on to payouts for weeks before releasing them.

item.title: Insurers Say French Supermarkets’ Cyber Insurance Unlikely to Cover Food Losses
item.description: French supermarkets are facing millions of euros in losses after a cyberattack forced them to throw away food, in a crisis that is not typically covered by cyber insurance policies but could still lead to higher premiums in the future, insurers told Reuters. Cyber insurance typically does not cover physical losses from attacks and supermarkets’ claims could be affected if they lacked the latest software updates, four insurance brokers told Reuters. Supermarkets’ cyber insurance policies may cover some costs, such as investigating internally or hiring PR advisors, but typically exclude physical losses.

item.title: Fintech Funding Fell 21% In Q3 As Deals Grew Scarcer
item.description: Venture funding into fintech startups slid 21.4% year over year in the third quarter of 2026, while deal count fell nearly 31%, Crunchbase data shows, pointing to a narrower funding market with fewer rounds and continued reliance on large transactions. Just 687 fintech funding rounds were recorded globally in the third quarter, compared with 789 in the previous quarter and 995 in the same period a year earlier. Funding from rounds of at least $100 million fell 43.3%, from $9.07 billion in Q2 to $5.15 billion in Q3, accounting for approximately 93% of the overall dollar decline.

item.title: How To Build A Billion-Dollar Company Without Venture Capital
item.description: I built a company into a multibillion-dollar business without any venture funding. Today’s venture capital ecosystem looks markedly different from even just five years ago. Most significantly, a small number of AI companies are now attracting the vast majority of available venture capital.

item.title: Deepening cat bond market offers investors liquidity, scale, and broader diversification: GAM’s Aviv
item.description: The catastrophe bond market has reached a scale where its continued growth actively reinforces the investment case, offering greater scalability, improved liquidity and broader scope to diversify within natural catastrophe risk, according to Dr. In a recent article authored by Aviv, the executive states that while natural catastrophe events are unpredictable, the behaviour of the cat bond market has historically exhibited a consistent pattern, one that underpins the asset class’s investment case. With the outstanding catastrophe bond market reaching $65.6 billion in H1 2026 , it’s increasing depth is delivering benefits to investors.

item.title: Jamaica’s parametric cat bond payout funded electricity restoration: Chief Fiscal Economist, Francis
item.description: After the devastating impacts of hurricane Melissa triggered a full $150 million payout of its IBRD CAR Jamaica 2024 parametric catastrophe bond, the rapid funding from this insurance product helped the country recover its electricity network faster than would have otherwise been possible, the government’s Chief Fiscal Economist explained last week. Speaking at the ILS Bermuda Convergence 2026 conference on the island last week, Terron Francis, Chief Fiscal Economist in the Ministry of Finance & the Public Service, Government of Jamaica highlighted the critical role of risk transfer and insurance risk capital in helping the Caribbean island nation to recover after the impactful storm. Francis said that the parametric catastrophe bond payout arrived within 30 days, supporting response and recovery for Jamaica, without forcing the government into emergency borrowing or substantial programme-budget reallocations.

item.title: Arbol launches parametric insurance for gov-imposed data center construction moratoriums
item.description: Arbol, the technology-led underwriter of parametric risk transfer, climate, and weather re/insurance business, has designed a parametric product that aims to transfer the risk of government-imposed moratoriums on data center construction projects. The parametric insurance is designed to protect against the regulatory risk of government halting or suspending data center construction as a class, rather than site-specific permit denials. Arbol’s new product is named Data Center Regulatory Moratorium Cover and it is seen as a beneficial addition to the data center insurance product complex, in being able to protect the capital already committed to a project and the carrying costs that can accumulate while construction efforts sit idle.

item.title: Rokstone expands Specialty Reinsurance team amid growth plans
item.description: Rokstone, an international managing general agent (MGA) specialising in specialty re/insurance, has appointed Airlie Isted ACII as an underwriter in its growing Specialty Reinsurance division. Her move to Rokstone also brings her back into a working relationship with Eddie Hughes, the company’s Head of Specialty Reinsurance, who first recruited her at Antares and has continued to follow her career. The appointment comes as Rokstone continues to expand its Specialty Reinsurance operation following its first year in business.

item.title: For legacy, discipline should sustain, not constrain growth: RiverStone International CEO
item.description: During a fireside chat at the annual AIRROC conference in New Jersey yesterday, Paul Brockman, CEO of legacy specialist RiverStone International, highlighted the difference in underwriting discipline between the live and retrospective markets, emphasising that discipline should sustain rather than constrain growth. Brockman, who joined RiverStone International as Group CEO from Enstar in January 2026 , explained that, alongside getting to know the company, its culture and its people, a main effort since taking on the role has been shifting the focus from a reactive to a proactive approach, a vision shared by his colleagues. RiverStone International has been around for a long time now, and has been particularly successful over the last four, five years.

item.title: Munich Re’s American Modern names Homm President and CEO

She has a decade of leadership experience at American Modern across internal audit, accounting, regulatory compliance, and enterprise risk management.

Meanwhile, in South Carolina, a licensed insurance producer and sales manager, appointed with two life insurance companies, was charged Oct. item.title: Google Cloud Outage in UK Eases After Affecting Digital Banks, Public Sector Websites
item.description: Alphabet’s Google said on Tuesday its cloud services in the UK were back up after an hours-long outage that disrupted several financial firms and public-sector websites. In July, the UK brought Google Cloud, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services and Oracle under direct regulatory oversight as critical third-party suppliers to the financial sector, citing the risk that an outage at a major provider could disrupt multiple firms at once. The outage put the spotlight on concerns among UK and EU regulators about the financial sector’s growing dependence on a small number of external technology providers, particularly cloud firms that support critical banking services.

item.title: A$7.9bn bid: Daiichi Life offers to buy rest of Challenger
item.description: Daiichi Life Group has offered to buy the rest of Challenger in a bid that values the Australian firm at around A$7.9bn, the latest move by a Japanese insurer to expand abroad. Shares of Challenger jumped as much as 18% in Sydney trading on Monday, while Daiichi Life was up about 1% in Tokyo.

item.title: 3M to Argue Australia’s $1.4 Billion ‘Forever Chemicals’ Lawsuit Legally Flawed
item.description: conglomerate 3M plans to argue a landmark case brought by Australia over contamination from the company’s use of PFAS “forever chemicals” in its firefighting foam is legally flawed, a court heard on Friday. The claim against the Minnesota-based chemicals maker and its local unit is the largest ever brought by Australia, and seeks more than A$2 billion ($1.38 billion) in damages for past and future costs of contamination across 28 military bases where 3M’s products were used. Australia’s case is that 3M knew or ought to have known the foam it made and supplied could damage the environment and harm people, but it failed to warn the government.

item.title: The Importance of Patience, Persistence, and Proper Documentation in Surveillance Investigations
item.description: While surveillance is often associated with capturing a single significant moment on video, successful investigations frequently depend on something far less dramatic: patience, persistence, and the ability to recognize meaningful activity as it unfolds. View Series In the field of insurance investigations, surveillance can play a critical role in providing claims professionals with objective information when evaluating reported injuries and physical limitations. As a private investigator, I have learned that some of the most reliable documentation results from remaining observant, maintaining appropriate positioning, and recognizing that a subject’s activities can change unexpectedly throughout the day.

item.title: Why Medical Record Review Shouldn’t Restart When New Records Arrive
item.description: Whether your medical record review runs on AI, people or both, the process should answer one question: What’s new since I last looked? View Series New medical records can come in months or years after a claim opens, so a summary that was written in March may be out of date by July. For claims managers looking at new technology and existing processes, it’s worth testing how the review holds up after several rounds of new records to see whether earlier work carries forward or the process starts over each time.

item.title: Clear exit terms and liquid collateral key to lowering casualty sidecar tail risk charges: AM Best
item.description: As casualty sidecars continue to gain traction, rating agency AM Best has highlighted that clear exit mechanics, high-quality collateral, and transparent risk transfer are critical to lowering tail risk capital charges for sponsors, warning that uncertain exit terms or weak collateral can leave cedents holding unexpected residual risk. The agency importantly states that tail risk matters on both sides of casualty sidecar transactions, given that investors want finality, and cedents want to know what risks (if any), are commuted back to them when an exit is exercised. AM Best added that Compre participates in a defined portion of the George Street Re sidecar, helping shape the contractual terms and the collateral construct that will govern at exit, and is positioned to step into the other investors’ positions over roughly five to seven years, with the ability to take on their future liabilities annually.
